description: No confirmed bulk/API access for the NBS supervised-entity register or the decisions register; the decisions listing appears to be a filtered HTML table.

ORSR and Obchodný vestník collection both require a watchlist of IČOs/ORSR IDs for every licensed SK bank, foreign-bank branch, payment institution and e-money institution. Only two example ORSR IDs were observed (VÚB, SZRB).
The NBS decisions filter exposes 'oblasť rozhodnutia' and 'druh rozhodnutia' facets whose allowed values were not enumerated in this pass.
Named individuals in regulatory decisions and commercial-register extracts are personal data; NBS/ORSR terms of use and any anonymisation practice were not reviewed.
This cell covers appointments and governance changes but produces no signal on rank-and-file hiring volume, job postings or team build-out at SK banks and PSPs.
I did not establish the settled Slovak term set NBS uses for PSD2/EMI key function holders as opposed to banks' 'vedúci zamestnanec priamo podriadený štatutárnemu orgánu'.
No concrete watchlist of SK bank / payment-institution / fintech IČOs was assembled in this pass; candidates are the plumbing, not the actor list.

Coverage of organizačná zložka / pobočka zahraničnej banky (branches of foreign banks and EU payment firms passporting into SK) is asserted but not demonstrated — no branch-specific register view was located.
It is unclear how far back ORSR 'úplný výpis' exposes deleted officers, and RÚZ is documented as mandatory only from accounting period 2013 onwards.
The Obchodný vestník 'Konkurzy a reštrukturalizácie' section was seen in search results but not examined as a distinct sub-stream, and no separate SK insolvency register was assessed.

English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature: orsr.sk, registeruz.sk, rpvs.gov.sk and Obchodný vestník are Slovak-only in substance, with only BRIS/e-Justice and vendor marketing pages in English.
Member-list deep URLs for SLASPO, SOPK, SAPIE innovator map, AFISP committees and AHK Slovakia were inferred from homepages/search snippets rather than fetched.

Conference and event speaker lists — explicitly the richest 'name + current title + employer' artefact for this cell — were not systematically enumerated (SBA events, AmCham/Britcham event portals, SAPIE and ITAS conferences, Fintech Matrix/ Slovak fintech events).

Trade-union side of the banking sector (odborové zväzy in banking, counterpart to SBA's employee-rights memorandum) was not scouted, and no regional-chamber (SOPK regional offices) officeholder lists were collected.
German-language (de) coverage for AHK Slovakia was only touched via one query; Hungarian-minority business associations in southern SK were not searched at all.

Members-only areas of chambers and associations (committee rosters, member directories behind login, Glue Up member portals) are the layer with the most named-officeholder detail but are not openly collectable.
No confirmed public SBA-run banking congress; the association's own event channel is unmapped.
Event detail pages and programme PDFs (ZBK, IBV NBS, NBS) were not opened in this pass; only listing levels were confirmed.
Historical speaker rosters (needed for the year-over-year title diff that makes this cell valuable) were not located; organiser sites typically overwrite the current edition.
University career fairs (EUBA, STU, UK, TUKE) are unsourced — no exhibitor lists found.
CEE regional conferences that host Slovak speakers (Future Banking Summit Brasov, Czech/Hungarian/Polish banking and card conferences) were only touched at the edge.
ATM/cash-cycle and self-service function holders in SK have no regional conference stage.
No source located in this pass for the governance/appointment record of the vláda SR session itself (rokovania.gov.sk) where SZRB/Eximbanka/Sociálna poisťovňa appointments are formally decided.
Cash-handling / CIT (cash-in-transit) and ATM-estate tenders by state-linked actors were not systematically explored; only card acquiring and payment gateways were.
No Hungarian-language or Roma-community-facing public-sector channels were checked, and no English-language SK government payment-procurement mirror beyond TED was identified.
It is unclear which ÚVO datasets in the national open-data catalogue actually carry contact-person fields, versus requiring notice-level HTML parsing.
Other state-adjacent financial actors were not explored: Slovenská konsolidačná, Slovak Investment Holding / SZRB Asset Management, VšZP (mass payment flows), and regional VÚC treasuries.
Accenture SK, IBM Slovensko, DXC Slovakia and Ness/other Kosice delivery centres have no confirmed reference or newsroom source in this slice.
LinkedIn — where most 'we welcome our new Slovakia FS lead' posts actually appear — was not collected, and is ToS-restricted for automated scraping.
SK-language IT trade press (itnews.sk, touchit.sk, nextech, PC Revue, Trend) was only reached indirectly via a vendor clipping page and not enumerated as sources in its own right.
No URL in this slice was fetched for liveness; several are inferred index pages (e.g. KPMG media index, PwC aktualne-spravy index, FinReport /lidri/) derived from observed article URLs.
Vendor case studies frequently anonymise the client bank, so programme-to-bank attribution is weak.
Case-level mass-redundancy notifications are not public; only aggregates.
The list of základné organizácie (in-bank union locals) of OZ PPaP and OZBP across all SK banks and payment firms was not enumerated; only Slovenská sporiteľňa locals were observed.
Individual regional labour offices (úrady práce, sociálnych vecí a rodiny) publish local notices and their own pages; none were individually assessed beyond one Trenčín-hosted procedural document.
Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA) is a central actor in the bargaining dispute but was reached only through third-party reporting, not through its own site in this pass.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin and largely supranational (Eurofound, EU-OSHA); no SK-focused English union or labour-law feed was found.
Žilina, Banská Bystrica, Nitra and Prešov are effectively uncovered — no city-specific source for financial-sector delivery centres was identified beyond national portals.
A definitive list of banking/payments captives and BPO providers with regional Slovak sites has not been assembled; only DT IT Solutions and DT Services Europe were concretely tied to Košice.
No company-registry or financial-statement source (ORSR, Finstat, registeruz) was evaluated in this pass, though these disclose employee counts and registered branch addresses by city.
Leadership-move signal for regional centre heads (site directors, centre GMs) is only weakly covered — LinkedIn is the natural source but is ToS-blocked for automated collection.
Several URLs were inferred from search-result metadata rather than fetched in this pass (e.g. SARIO news index, EKF TUKE root, KSK site root).
Within the cell's named actor list, Oberbank Slovensko and mBank SK were resolved only to a site root / group press room; no SK-level management ('vedenie', 'o nás') page was confirmed for either.

Careers/ATS pages were confirmed only for SLSP and VÚB. The equivalent 'kariéra / voľné pracovné miesta' hubs for Tatra banka, ČSOB SK, 365.bank, Prima banka, UniCredit SK, mBank SK, Oberbank SK and J&T Banka were not individually resolved in this pass.
No RSS/Atom or sitemap.xml endpoints were identified for any of the newsrooms in this cell; every candidate is currently specified as an HTML crawl.
Management-page diffing only detects change from the moment snapshotting begins; there is no historical baseline of who held which portfolio before the run started.
The cell's actor list excludes second-tier SK banks that surfaced repeatedly during searching (Privatbanka, Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka / SZRB) and which do publish leadership changes.
UniCredit's CZ&SK press centre was reached only through its /en/ path with Czech-derived URL segments (tiskove-centrum/tiskove-zpravy); the Slovak-language variant was not confirmed.
Non-bank payment firms with foreign listed parents operating in Slovakia (acquirers, card schemes, PSPs, ATM operators) were not covered; the pass was bank-dominated.
Group-level careers/HR channels of the parents were not scouted, only IR/press channels.
The Belgian (FSMA/STORI) and Italian (CONSOB / eMarket SDIR-STORAGE) officially appointed mechanisms for KBC and Intesa were not identified, unlike Austria's OeKB IIC.

The core premise — that parent English disclosure precedes Slovak subsidiary communication — is asserted but only anecdotally testable so far (the SLSP CEO case appears same-day on both erstegroup.com and slsp.sk).
The Slovak supervisory side of appointments (NBS fit-and-proper approvals, which every appointment found is conditioned on) was out of this cell's scope and is unassigned here.
The CSOB / 365.bank legal and operational merger is the dominant forthcoming SK org-change event and currently rests on a single channel (KBC newsroom/IR).
SK-domiciled independent ATM deployers / ISOs beyond Euronet were not enumerated; the cell needs a full list of ATM operators registered or notified to NBS.
Košice and other regional SK delivery/shared-service locations of payments firms were not investigated; searching concentrated on Bratislava.
SK general business media (Trend/eTrend, Hospodárske noviny, Forbes.sk, Index SME, Touchit) were not individually assessed as monitored feeds for payments people-moves.
Scheme-side (Visa/Mastercard) CEE regional newsrooms and their CZ-language equivalents were not located; SK announcements likely originate there.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed live; all liveness/status assessments are hypotheses from search-result metadata.

The SK glossary built here is thin on employment-event verbs used in appointment reporting (e.g. 'vymenovaný do funkcie', 'novým riaditeľom sa stal', 'posilnil vedenie', 'ukončil pôsobenie', 'presúva pracovné miesta').
The Obchodný vestník URL was inferred rather than found in search results, and the ORSR search interface was not exercised. Both are central to the leadership-move tier.

The actor map is not yet enumerated. The PSD2 JSON register, the Slovak FinTech Association member list and the NBS crypto licensee set were all identified but not dereferenced into concrete company names in this pass.

Founder-level channels other than LinkedIn were not probed: X/Twitter accounts of SK fintech founders, company Facebook pages (the Slovak FinTech Association maintains an active one), podcasts and YouTube interviews. Slovak business podcasts often carry the first mention of a senior hire.

Talent-side intermediaries were not covered: SK fintech-focused recruiters and executive-search firms, and the sector salary surveys (Profesia publishes salary data) that reveal which roles are in demand.

Cross-border registers were not searched. Several SK fintechs operate via CZ, MT or LT entities — finby's reported Malta licence is a live example — so appointments may be filed with the MFSA, the Czech ARES/justice.cz register or the CNB rather than with SK authorities.

The three highest-recall sources for this cell's core signal — LinkedIn, FinStat MONITORING and the funding databases — are all login-walled, paid or ToS-restricted. Only the free register tier is collectable without commercial arrangements.

Several SK banking/payments actors have no identified hiring channel yet: Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka, Poštová banka (post-365 rebrand entity), mBank/Fio/Oberbank/J&T Banka SK branches, and PSD2 licensed payment institutions / e-money institutions registered with NBS.

Payments-infrastructure vendors and processors operating in SK (ATM/POS estate, card personalisation, switch operators, e.g. Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Voyix, Printec, Monet+, Nexi, Worldline) are not yet mapped to hiring channels.
Vacancy disappearance (a wind-down signal) and salary-band drift cannot be reconstructed retrospectively without a longitudinal archive.
Executive/leadership moves are barely covered by job boards — such roles are filled via executive search, not public postings.
No RSS/API/structured feed identified for any SK board; robots.txt and ToS posture unchecked.

LinkedIn company pages unmapped for VÚB, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, mBank SK, Privatbanka, Prima banka, SZRB, plus payments actors Worldline SK, Global Payments SK/Erste-JV entities and Mastercard/Visa SK country teams.
The post/activity layer (the actual 'excited to announce' announcements) is not reachable by the tooling used here; only static profile and company pages are.
No structured watchlist yet exists of SK banking/payments executives (CEOs, board members, heads of payments/cards/digital) and of the recruiters who place them.
No baseline headcount snapshot has been taken, so no trend can be computed for at least one collection cycle.
This cell is intrinsically personal-data heavy (named individuals, employment history) and LinkedIn's ToS prohibits automated collection.

Smaller SK-owned executive search boutiques (TARGET Executive Search, Personality Group, Perfect Personal, Jenewein/Talentor-type players) were only glimpsed via directories, not individually profiled.
LinkedIn — where SK recruiters actually post mandates, placements and market commentary — was not queried, and is the single richest intermediary channel for this cell.
Employer-branding awards beyond Najzamestnávateľ (e.g. Via Bona, AmCham/BSCC employer recognitions, Great Place to Work SK) were not checked for banking participants.
The authoritative SK executive-search ranking (Index/SME) is behind a partial paywall, so firm-level placement volumes could not be extracted.
No RSS/sitemap endpoints confirmed for any outlet in this cell; every candidate's collection method is currently a hypothesis.

Coverage found is Bratislava/national. Regional dailies (Korzar, MY regional titles) and specialist HR/labour titles that would report individual branch closures and district-level mass-layoff filings were not explored.

Most large Slovak banks are Czech- or Austrian/Italian-owned (Erste, Intesa, RBI, KBC, UniCredit). Czech and Austrian business press often break Slovak executive moves first, and this cell did not cover cs/de-language outlets.
Investigative outlets that would cover exits under pressure and disputes (e.g. Investigate.sk / ICJK, Aktuality.sk investigative desk) were not directly confirmed as candidates in this pass.
No URL in this slice has been confirmed reachable by this agent; two anchor domains actively failed to fetch.
